# A Scheduler backed by a task tree returns bookings for the wrong resource

## Context

The three-window planning demo needs the same leaf task to be a resource booking, a Gantt bar and a board card. The Gantt's expansion state is local to how a person reads its tree. It should not remove another person's booking from a scheduling view.

## The Problem

A real App Worker drive used a Gantt TaskStore with lighting assigned to Alpha and walls assigned to Beta. The Scheduler and Gantt resolved lighting to the same object. Asking the store for the date range and resource Alpha returned **both** lighting and walls. The generic event-store query returned only lighting. Collapsing the Build phase dropped the visible population from 15 to 11; both visible-range queries then omitted lighting, although `store.get('lighting')` still returned the identical record.

The probe ran on the phase-rollup candidate. The relevant range method and Scheduler dispatch were compared with the committed Engine source.

## The Architectural Reality

[`timeline.Column`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/50fcfc526c/src/timeline/Column.mjs#L1003) calls an event store's range method with a resource ID. [`TaskStore#getRangeRecords`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/50fcfc526c/src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs#L29) documents two arguments and intentionally enumerates expanded visible rows. [`Events.getRangeRecords`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/50fcfc526c/src/timeline/store/Events.mjs#L80) is resource-aware but also enumerates the supplied population. Both contracts serve existing callers.

## The Fix

Provide a supported path for the Scheduler to query the intended bookings by time and resource independently of Gantt tree expansion. Preserve canonical record identity and the two-argument Gantt visible-range contract. A provider-owned projection is a candidate if it can meet those semantics and lifetime/cost controls. Record the chosen owner before implementation.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TaskStore#getBookingStore()` | The TaskStore owns task identity and structural membership. Scheduler and Board borrow its leaf records. | Lazily returns one `Neo.timeline.store.Events` for the live TaskStore. Its entries are the same task instances and its filters are independent of tree visibility. | Reads include folded tasks. The owner reconciles structural writes, including silent ones, and destroys the view on teardown. Consumers write scheduling changes through the Gantt operation. | [Gantt guide](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/763c09aa85595da113b868eec6c3dfed60ae48b2/learn/guides/datahandling/Gantt.md), [method JSDoc](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/763c09aa85595da113b868eec6c3dfed60ae48b2/src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs) | [TaskStore unit suite](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/763c09aa85595da113b868eec6c3dfed60ae48b2/test/playwright/unit/gantt/TaskStore.spec.mjs), [three-window gestures](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/763c09aa85595da113b868eec6c3dfed60ae48b2/test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/SharedPlanning.spec.mjs) |
| `TaskStore#getRangeRecords(start, end, resourceId)` | Existing Gantt visible-row reads and the Scheduler resource-specific range contract | A supplied non-null resource ID selects the matching leaf bookings in the booking view. | Omit the resource or pass `null` to retain the two-argument Gantt visible-row semantics. Dates follow the underlying event range rules. | [Range method](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/763c09aa85595da113b868eec6c3dfed60ae48b2/src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs) | Same suites, including two resource rows, collapse, reassign and independent filters. |

At candidate `763c09aa85`, a local Node fixture with 20 collapsed phases, 2,000 leaves and 10 resources created the booking view in 2.92 ms. Expand and collapse of one phase took 0.62 ms. After 10 warmups, 100 date-and-resource reads returned 200 matches with median 0.185 ms and p95 0.345 ms. These are measurements from this machine. [Source PR](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/22013).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With Alpha and Beta bookings at the same time, both the Scheduler's public range read and its painted resource rows contain only their respective leaf bookings.
- [ ] Collapsing a phase hides its children in Gantt and leaves its bookings visible on Scheduler. Expanding it brings back the same record instances; task updates, date boundaries and resource moves stay correct.
- [ ] Existing two-argument Gantt reads preserve their visible-row semantics. A caller intentionally filtering bookings can still do so independently of tree expansion.
- [ ] No second population of writable domain records or window message relay is introduced. Measure the query on a representative tree and cover the owning store's teardown.

## Out of Scope

The separate question of who schedules successor dependencies after a Scheduler drag, and the demo's visual design.

const store = Neo.create(TaskStore, {data: [

const edges = Neo.create(DependencyStore, {data: [{id: 'ab', fromId: 'a', toId: 'b', type: 'FS'}]});
const timeAxis = {timeZone: 'UTC', start: at(0), end: at(24), snapMinutes: 15};
const gantt = Neo.create(Gantt, {appName, store, dependencyStore: edges, timeAxis});
const scheduler = Neo.create(Scheduler, {appName, eventStore: store, store: resources, timeAxis});

const ids = rows => rows.map(task => task.id);

    console.log('same task:', gantt.resolveTaskRecord('a') === a && scheduler.resolveEventRecord('a') === a);
    console.log('scheduler, Alpha:', ids(scheduler.getResourceEvents('alpha', at(0), at(8))));
    console.log('resource-filter control:', ids(Events.getRangeRecords(store, at(0), at(8), 'alpha')));

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-22T19:17:54Z

The shared planning candidate uses a lazily owned booking store on `Neo.gantt.TaskStore`. It holds the canonical leaf record references but owns an independent Model and filter. The owning task store forwards record and batch updates. Scheduler and Board borrow that same booking view; Gantt keeps its visible tree-row range semantics. An explicit resource range on the TaskStore selects bookings for that resource. A `sourceId` copy of the visible tree lost the booking on collapse, and passing the same Model instance retargeted record-change delivery, so neither is the implementation. I’m checking silent structural writes and cross-window rendering before publishing the branch with #21915.
